reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend shifting, but repeats daily exclusion policy across getNextDate and both server handlers instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Daily non-working-day checks and skip-versus-shift dispatch are repeated across the handlers and the forward and fallback paths in getNextDate.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handlers also own scheduling policy that should live alongside it.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration propagation, or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Multiple policy implementations and independently chosen enumeration limits make future scheduling changes require coordinated edits across several paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange reproduce the shared non-working-day predicate; createScheduleList retains two raw getNextDate(..., true) calls followed by shifting, bypassing the daily exclusion policy in getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily exclusion decision appears as iterative occurrence selection in getNextDate and flatMap filtering in both handlers, while the handlers inline the predicate encapsulated by isNonWorkingDay.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate adds daily-specific forward filtering, fallback rejection, and shift suppression; two handler transformations and two budget-template raw-occurrence/shift sites keep policy outside a unified shared definition.
